about.heading: I got here by taking things apart
body: I'm a final-year information technology student in Pune. My way into software wasn't a childhood obsession with computers — it was a stubborn need to know how the things I used every day actually worked. That curiosity turned into servers, ledgers, and the occasional small tool I needed and nobody had written yet.

Most of what I know came from rebuilding something that already existed. Writing a Redis-compatible server in C++ taught me more about memory and concurrency than any course did. Building a payments ledger forced me to care about the boring, important parts: idempotency, ordering, and what happens when the network drops halfway through a transaction.

Right now I'm looking for a software engineering placement where I can work on systems at a scale I can't simulate on my own laptop. I care about code someone else can read at 2am, and about shipping things that actually reach people.
